what: Deep frames as the explorer's CPU kernel draws them: the website's committed perturb-scalar.wasm over every parity spec at its own grid and over every Deep gallery link at 32x18, ss 1 — a parity spec as it is written, a gallery link at a cold open (no held reference, no period) — and engine.wasm's shade_level colouring each field. Each case carries the spec as the page builds it, `lanes` (FNV-1a-64 over the little-endian f64 lanes, rows in order over the whole frame, NaN for interior), `ran`/`saved` (the band counters after that one whole-frame call), `nan` (FNV over one byte a sample, 1 where the lane is NaN), `values` (the lane bytes, base64), and `rgb`/`pixels` (FNV and base64 of the shaded picture with alpha stripped). Parity specs carry no colour and are shaded by `shade_link`; a gallery link without `scale` records `rgb: null` and `why`, as render-link refuses it, and so would a field engine.wasm's shade_level trapped on (none does). The Rust test parses each `spec`, draws it natively with compute_rows, and holds `nan`, `ran` and `saved` exactly and `lanes` and `rgb` exactly or within its stated tolerance. Regenerated by running `generator` under node with the fractal-website checkout as its argument (and `--specs <path>` for the parity specs); `contract_blobs` names the git blob of each file it read.
